title: Application Context V2.5
description: The Application Context of an application served by JSON Interface (MMC-JSI): the standing description of the application, given to the AIM through its Access (Settings CommandSchema, ResponseSchema and ApplicationContext). CommandSchema and ResponseSchema are the schemas of the commands and of the responses of the application; this schema is the structure of the Application Context beyond them, which says what those two schemas do not. A path in a guide is a dotted path from the name of a command or response, through its properties, to the property or object it designates (for example UserCommandRQ.MovedObjects.Objects.ObjectID). Only Header is required: every other member is a help that an implementation of JSON Interface may use.

Path.description: A dotted path in the command or response schema.

WordList.description: Words or phrases, in lower case, that are looked for in a request.

Command.description: A command, an instance of the CommandSchema.

Description.description: Says which application the Application Context is for and where it is kept in the Access of the implementation.

Application.description: What the application is and does, in words, given to the language model.

Conventions.description: What the schemas do not say and the commands rely on: units, axes, orientations, which field a verb is for, how a change by an amount is made, other words for an object.

Include.description: The paths of the command schema that the request is allowed to fill. Everything else is left out of the schema given to the model, to make it small.

Require.description: Paths that are required in the schema given to the model, though the command schema does not require them.

Drop.description: Paths removed from the schema given to the model.

Skip.description: Names of properties that are not shown in the descriptions of the response, because they carry no meaning for the person.

Generated.description: Names of properties that the AIM gives a value to after the model has answered (identifiers, times): the model is not asked for them.

Fill.description: Values the AIM sets in a command: a path, or a property name, and the value; {id} is a new identifier and {now} the time.

Names.description: Paths whose value is the name of an object, and the set of names that the value is taken from.

Set.description: Members: the objects of the open scene; Present: the open scene and its objects; Stored: the objects kept and not yet used.

NeedsObject.description: Requests that act on an object and name none are not turned into a command: the person is asked.

Paths.description: The commands that need an object.

Names.description: The sentence that lists the names, with {0} for the list.

Synonyms.description: Another word and the name it stands for.

Unless.description: Commands that do not need an object.

Anything.description: Words that stand for the whole scene.

NeedsNumber.description: Requests that say an amount without a number are not turned into a command: the person is asked.

Phrases.description: Phrases that call for an amount.

Refusals.description: Requests that are not for the application.

Problem.description: What the AIM says when the request has one of the words.

Triggers.description: Paths of the command schema kept, for a request, only when it has one of the words.

Hints.description: A sentence added to the request when it has one of the words.

Shortcuts.description: Requests that are answered with a fixed command, without the model.

StateRequests.description: The commands that ask the application for its state, sent when the AIM does not know it.

Context.description: How the state of the application is read from a response and told to the model.

Items.description: The path of the list of things in the response.

Name.description: The property that names an item.

Kind.description: The property that says what an item is.

Members.description: The property that counts the members of a scene.

MemberName.description: The property that names a member.

MemberNames.description: The property that lists the names of the members of a scene.

Describe.description: Values of an item that are told to the model.

Words.description: The sentences that tell the state: State, Scene ({0} the name, {1} the number of members), Stored, Unknown.

Earlier.description: The property of a command that names an earlier command (to undo it).

ResponseIntro.description: The first words of the Response Hint.

Words.description: The words with which the Response Hint tells a property or a value of a response.

Examples.description: Requests with the command they stand for, given to the model.

State.description: The state of the application that the example assumes.

Earlier.description: The commands sent before that the example assumes, one per line.

Working.description: The reasoning that leads to the command, or to the problem.

Problem.description: What is said instead of a command, when the request does not become one.

Descriptions.description: A description for a path, added to the description of the command schema.

Working.description: Whether the model writes its reasoning before the command.

Reminder.description: A sentence repeated to the model after the request.
